Class MarkupParser

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.text.MarkupParser
public final class MarkupParser extends Object
Parses BBCode-style markup text and converts it to styled Text objects.

The parser supports:

  • Built-in modifier tags: [bold], [italic], [underlined], [dim], [reversed], [crossed-out]
  • Built-in color tags: [red], [green], [blue], [yellow], [cyan], [magenta], [white], [black], [gray]
  • True color tokens: [#RGB], [#RRGGBB], [rgb(r,g,b)] (spaces allowed)
  • Compound style specs: multiple tokens in a single tag, e.g. [bold #ff5733 on rgb(10, 20, 30)]text[/]. Foreground/background tokens are parsed using ColorConverter and modifiers are applied in addition to colors.
  • Hyperlinks: [link=URL]text[/link]
  • Custom tags: resolved via a MarkupParser.StyleResolver
  • Escaped brackets: [[ produces [, and ]] produces ]
  • Nested tags: [red][bold]text[/bold][/red]
  • Emoji codes: :smiley:, :warning:, :success:, etc. (replaced with Unicode emoji)

Example usage: 

// Simple parsing with built-in styles
Text text = MarkupParser.parse("This is [red]red[/red] and [bold]bold[/bold].");

// With custom tag resolver
Text text = MarkupParser.parse(
    "This is [keyword]styled[/keyword].",
    tagName -> {
        if ("keyword".equals(tagName)) {
            return Style.EMPTY.fg(Color.CYAN).bold();
        }
        return null;
    }
);

Unknown tags without a resolver are rendered as plain text (tags are preserved). Unclosed tags apply their style to the remaining content.

    • parse

      public static Text parse(String markup)
      Parses markup text using only built-in styles.

      Custom tags are rendered as plain text (the tag markers are preserved). Emoji codes (e.g. :smiley:, :warning:) are replaced with Unicode emoji characters.

      Parameters:
      markup - the markup text to parse
      Returns:
      the parsed styled text
